decisions.reason: The evening day-patient program has its own page, draws on established psychiatric expertise and serves an insurer-funded need of working patients, so it costs little to keep while its demand becomes clear.
The carpentry workshop uses the existing sheltered-workshop infrastructure and staff, so the option is cheap to hold and still offers upside in custom furniture sales and meaningful work places.
Outpatient sociotherapy is reimbursable and close to the core psychiatric services, and its limited visibility signals remaining uncertainty rather than proven failure, which favors waiting.
The retail shop carries fixed costs and low visibility, but it complements the workshop's products and is still too new for its value to be judged, so the option stays open for another year.

The newly launched senior meal delivery leverages existing kitchens and eldercare clients at low incremental cost, and its early stage means uncertainty has not yet resolved enough to justify abandonment.
